change.title: pr-10
change.description: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding
change.author: Robin Ward

findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset (the default)
findings.body: `execute(...)[0]['id']` assumes the JOIN returns a row. `embed_category` defaults to '' (config/site_settings.yml before this change), so on most sites no `site_settings` row exists or no category matches. The result is empty, `[0]` is nil or raises, and the migration aborts. Line 15 has the same problem: `uncategorized_category_id` is only in `site_settings` if it was stored there explicitly. Check `cmd_tuples`/`ntuples` before indexing, and fall back to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` or a lookup in `categories`.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are not normalized and are interpolated into SQL
findings.body: The old `allows_embeddable_host?` accepted entries like `http://eviltrout.com` or ones with paths, because it stripped the scheme and parsed with URI. This migration inserts the raw lines, which can keep a scheme, a path, a trailing `\r` or spaces. `record_for_host` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17) compares only against `uri.host`, so these sites silently stop accepting embeds after the upgrade. The value is also interpolated straight into SQL: a quote breaks the migration. Strip the scheme, path and whitespace, and quote the value (`ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote`).

findings.title: before_validation raises on nil host
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil, for example when the client omits `host` in `params[:embeddable_host]` (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23). The result is a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `return if host.blank?` or use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

findings.title: Case-insensitive lookup only lowercases one side
findings.body: `lower(host) = ?` is compared with `uri.host` as given, and the referer is not downcased. A referer with uppercase letters (`http://EvilTrout.com/`) never matches, even though the stored value would. Use `host.downcase`.

findings.title: Hosts with a port validate but can never match
findings.body: The format regex accepts `example.com:8080`, and before_validation strips only the scheme and path, so the port is kept. `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, which never includes a port, so such a record never allows anything. Either drop the port from the regex or strip it before saving.

findings.title: Unknown id gives a 500 on update/destroy
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first` returns nil for a stale or unknown id. Then `host.destroy` or `save_host(nil)` raises NoMethodError. Use `find` (404) or `raise Discourse::NotFound`.

findings.title: Delete failure is silent
findings.body: `destroyRecord()` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, unlike `save` at line 40. If the request fails, nothing tells the admin and the row stays as if the click did nothing.

findings.title: `_ids` keys with null values crash hydration
findings.body: Any payload key ending in `_ids` is now treated as an array, and `obj[k].map` throws if the value is null or not an array. `hydrated || []` never applies, because `map` always returns an array. Guard with `(obj[k] || [])`.

findings.title: update action does nothing
findings.body: `update` only re-renders, and the client's `saveChanges` (admin-embedding.js.es6:6) sends `{}`. No template calls it. Remove both or implement them.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped
findings.body: category_fabricator.rb now defines `:embeddable_host`, and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators. It works only because all fabricators load, but finding them is confusing. Swap the contents back.

findings.title: Test name no longer matches what it tests
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer looks at embeddable hosts, so "is false if embeddable_host is blank" passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false and `has_topic_embed?` is false. Rename the test or remove it. The `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` in the nested `before` is also irrelevant.

findings.title: find('fruit', 2) actually gets fruit 1
findings.body: The pretender `/fruits/:id` always returns `fruits[0]` (create-pretender.js.es6:227), which is apple with color_ids [1,2]. The test asks for id 2 (banana, color_ids [3]) and asserts apple's colors, so it reads as if it checks banana. Request id 1, or make the pretender honour the id.

findings.title: Truncation no longer gated on hosts being configured
findings.body: Before, `expandable_first_post?` was gated on `embeddable_hosts` being present. Now it no longer checks whether any host is configured. With embed_truncate on and no hosts, existing embedded topics still show as expandable.

contracts.action: Migration converts embeddable_hosts/embed_category settings into rows and deletes the settings
contracts.before_after: Before: hosts were read from the setting with scheme/path tolerance. After: rows are stored raw, the settings are deleted unconditionally, and lookups match exact lowercase host only.
contracts.visible_effect: Embeds from hosts configured with a scheme or path stop working after the upgrade
contracts.failure_mode: The DELETE runs even when the inserts stored values that will never match. On an empty category lookup the migration crashes before reaching it.

contracts.visible_effect: The row is removed from the list on success
contracts.failure_mode: No catch, so a failed delete is silent. The server raises a 500 if the id is unknown.

contracts.before_after: Before: the category came from the embed_category name. After: it comes from the integer category_id, found by id.
contracts.visible_effect: Embedded topics are posted to the host's category
contracts.failure_mode: nil if no matching host, so the topic is uncategorized

summary: This PR moves the list of allowed embed hosts from site settings into a new table with its own admin screen. It has one blocker: the migration indexes `[0]` on a query result that is empty whenever `embed_category` is unset, which is the default, so the migration crashes on most sites. The migration also copies host values unnormalized, and the new lookup no longer tolerates a scheme or path, so some sites lose embedding silently after the upgrade. Smaller issues: the model raises on a nil host, a lowercase comparison only lowercases one side, and admin delete failures and unknown ids are not handled. There are also some test and fabricator cleanups.
